prompt: Our email-sending service uses one shared BullMQ queue for two kinds of jobs: bulk "newsletter" jobs (low priority, ~30s of work each) and urgent "reset-password" jobs (enqueued with priority: 1, the highest possible). The team assumed giving reset-password the top priority number would make it start almost immediately. In production, during a newsletter burst, a user requested a password reset and the email arrived about 29 seconds late — logs confirm the job was enqueued with priority 1 but still sat waiting before its handler started. Below is the relevant queue module, processor, and producers. Debug why the priority-1 job was delayed, and propose a structural fix (don't blame the priority number or Redis's scoring itself).
